ticket.title: Make the verifier stricter than the generator: compile is too easy a bar
ticket.description:
The owner observed that Gold is rare partly because the oracle and the universal provider are the same model - the verifier cannot be harder than the generator. There is a cheaper lever than harder fixtures: raise the verifiers bar.

Today assess_rust + miter verify accept anything that compiles. A candidate that compiles but ignores the documented delegation, leaves an unused import, or returns a wrong-but-well-typed value passes as Silver, and no repair happens. Measured consequence: sum_positive produced 0/3 Gold because its one-line delegation compiles first try.

PROPOSAL: grade the oracle in tiers and let a caller pick - (1) compiles, (2) compiles + clippy -D warnings (unused imports and dead code become failures), (3) compiles + the crates tests pass, (4) compiles + a property or doc-test assertion when the fixture provides one. Tier 2 alone would have rejected the unicode_segmentation candidate on the unused-import rule and forced the repair that the doc comment was asking for. This manufactures Gold honestly - by demanding more, not by inventing difficulty - and it is measurable: same fixtures, compare tier-1 vs tier-2 Gold rate.
